topics.topic: Whether first-lock bootstrap may create missing parent folders when only lock creation is permitted
questions: When acquiring a project's lock for the first time requires creating folders below the state folder, are those folders permitted writes under A3's exception for the project lock, or must an operation that later fails conditions 1 to 4 create only the lock file?
When folders leading to a first lock are absent, may the operation create those folders as well as the lock, or must “the only write” mean exactly one filesystem entry?

When a delivery reaches the project lock and its lock-file folders do not yet exist, may it create those folders before later failing under A3 conditions 1 to 4, or is the lock file itself the only permitted new filesystem entry?
Does “that first creation” mean only creation of the lock file, or the complete bootstrap consisting of the lock file and every newly created folder leading to it?

quotes:
Conditions 1 to 4 write nothing except the
   project lock (A6 rule 4).

The lock file is created on first
   use with the imported `LOCK_FILE_MODE` constant, and the folders below the state folder that lead to
   it with the mode rule 2 decides; the lock file is never changed or removed afterwards; that first creation is the
   only write of an operation that writes nothing else.
judgement.why: A3 permits only the project lock to be written on an early failed delivery, while A6 requires missing leading folders to be created yet calls creation of the lock file the operation's only write.

witness.initial: The installation-created state folder exists, but the folders leading to a project's lock and the lock file do not exist.
events: A caller requests delivery of a name whose final segment is absent.
The deliverer passes the checks before the project lock and reaches the project-lock step.
The deliverer bootstraps the lock path and then evaluates the named file, which fails condition 1.
outcomes: Under A6's folder-creation rule, the service creates the leading folders and lock file, then answers NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT.
Under A3's and A6's only-write language, the service may create only the lock file, so it must refuse at lock acquisition or require the leading folders to pre-exist.
witness.observer: The caller sees success through the lock step versus refusal, and the owner sees whether leading folders were created.
basis:
One call delivers one photo, named by `name`, a relative path in the form a scan reports, and
   `source_id`.

Checks run in this order: token, request form and project id, connection, photo folder, source id,
   project lock, existing placement, named file.

The installation creates the binary
   store and the state folder; the service creates only folders below them, with the imported
   `STORE_FOLDER_MODE` and `STATE_FOLDER_MODE` constants, and removes none.

questions: What authoritative time source supplies marked_at when a publication mark is created?

quotes:
The system clock is the one source of the current time, declared as `rules.time_source_policy`
   and reaching code through `system_clock_backend` as the operation `utc_now`.

The current time is a `datetime` in UTC without an offset, with microsecond precision and no
   rounding, written in ISO 8601 form as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, followed by `.` and six digits when
   the microseconds are not zero, with no offset. Every instant of a record and an answer is written
   so. It sets `marked_at`.
judgement.why: P2 already judged the same authoritative-source question on the same time rules.

precedent.topic: Clock source, representation, timezone, and read count for marked_at
quotes:
The system clock is the one source of the current time, declared as `rules.time_source_policy`
   and reaching code through `system_clock_backend` as the operation `utc_now`.

Only a mark reads it, once, after the token, the request form and the identifiers are accepted and
   before the connection is examined or the project lock is taken. A mark refused before that point does
   not read it. A mark refused after it, and a replayed mark, have read it and write nothing. Scan, delivery
   and the health answer never read it.

The current time is a `datetime` in UTC without an offset, with microsecond precision and no
   rounding, written in ISO 8601 form as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, followed by `.` and six digits when
   the microseconds are not zero, with no offset. Every instant of a record and an answer is written
   so. It sets `marked_at`.
precedent.why: A7 identifies the clock authority, fixes the single sampling point and read count, and specifies the exact UTC-naive microsecond representation and serialization.

topics.topic: Camera metadata conditions that trigger modification-time fallback
questions: Exactly which camera-record conditions trigger the modification-time fallback: absence only, or also malformed, out-of-range, contradictory, or timezone-incomplete metadata?

quotes:
The photo moment is the first usable value of: EXIF `DateTimeOriginal`, EXIF `DateTime`, then
   the file's modification time. `DateTimeOriginal` uses `OffsetTimeOriginal` when that offset has
   the form `+HH:MM` or `-HH:MM` with hours up to 14 and minutes up to 59; otherwise it is read in the time zone of the `timezone` field of the run settings (A8), and so is
   `DateTime`. A camera value is unusable when it is malformed, when its UTC year
   is before 2000, or when it is more than 24 hours after the file's modification time.
judgement.why: A2 defines the fallback order, the unusable-camera-value conditions, and how an absent or invalid offset is handled.

topics.topic: UTC conversion of camera timestamps without an offset
questions: How is a camera timestamp that carries no UTC offset converted to UTC?

quotes:
The photo date is delivered as UTC without an offset, as the Client Portal stores it. A camera
   time with no offset is read in the time zone of that `timezone` field. A local time that occurs twice is the
   first occurrence, and a local time that does not exist is read with the offset in force before
   the clock change. A modification time is an absolute instant converted to UTC.
judgement.why: A2 specifies the configured run timezone and resolves both ambiguous and nonexistent local camera times before conversion to offsetless UTC.
